keywords: binary search searching sorted list array algorithm find halving divide logarithmic complexity
facts: Binary search only works on sorted data.
It compares the target with the middle element.
Each step throws away half of the remaining items.
It needs about log2(n) steps, so its time complexity is O(log n).
For 1,000 items it needs about 10 steps; for 1,000,000 about 20.

scenes.heading: Binary search
scenes.subtitle: Find a value fast in a sorted list

narration.text: Binary search finds a value in a sorted list by cutting the search in half each time.
First, look at the middle item of the list.
If the target is bigger, throw away the left half.
If it is smaller, throw away the right half.
Repeat on the half that is left, until you find it.

scenes.heading: Step 2: The code
scenes.code:
def search(nums, target):
    low, high = 0, len(nums) - 1
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        if nums[mid] == target: return mid
        if nums[mid] < target: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
    return -1

narration.text: Low and high mark the two ends of the search area.
Mid is the middle position. If it holds the target, we return it.
If the middle value is too small, we move low up to search the right half.
Otherwise we move high down to search the left half.

scenes.heading: Step 3: Why it is so fast

narration.text: Each step halves the list, so even huge lists need few steps.
Eight items need only three halvings.
A thousand items need about ten steps.
A million items need only about twenty.
A linear search may check all one thousand items.
Binary search needs only about ten checks.
We say binary search runs in logarithmic time, written O of log n.

scenes.answer: Found at index 4 after only 2 checks

narration.text: We search for twenty three in a sorted list of six numbers.
The middle item is fifteen, which is too small.
So we throw away the left half and keep sixteen, twenty three and forty two.
The new middle is twenty three: found in just two checks.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: Binary search only works on which kind of list?

narration.text: Quick check. What kind of list does binary search need?
A sorted list. Cutting in half only works when values are in order.

scenes.heading: Quick check
scenes.question: About how many steps for 1,000 sorted items?

narration.text: Quick check. About how many steps for a thousand items?
About ten, because two to the power ten is about a thousand.
